- Policy stance: The FOMC maintained a highly accommodative posture (near-zero rates, ongoing Treasury and agency MBS purchases) to support market functioning and credit flows.
- Beige Book cross-check: Reports of only modest growth with renewed COVID-related headwinds; employment gains slowed and activity remained below pre-pandemic levels. Contacts cited disruptions to shippers and producers, supply chain bottlenecks, and heightened uncertainty.
- Credit conditions: Consistent with SLOOS, the Beige Book noted tighter lending standards and softer loan demand for businesses (C&I and CRE), while housing demand stayed strong amid low mortgage rates. Transmission remains uneven, with riskier borrowers facing more friction.
- Prices: Inflation pressures were subdued overall, though some input costs rose due to logistics and supply constraints.
Net assessment: Despite supportive policy, Beige Book anecdotes about virus resurgence, supply-chain/logistics disruptions, and tighter credit for firms temper the outlook more than the SLOOS-only view.
